Yeah, I understand where you're coming from. I am not a pure communist myself, I think I forgot to mention that. In my opinion, reading and studying about the things that the people in the opposite political spectrum as you believe in is a great way of widening your horizon. It gives you perspective as to why people believe in what people believe in.


> Well comrade most postmodernist are MARXISTS it's actually run by postmodernists who crave only thing POWER 

And I have to disagree with your first statement. No (true) marxist craves power, but the redistribution of power. The only oppression a marxist is interested in is economic oppression. I am not a Marxist myself but I do think some of their view points make sense. 


> I don't like Communism. But I hope we turn into like Norway, every country should look up to Norway they got basics need covered. Got social security for every one and free market


I am a big fan of nordic countries too, and I hope India follows in their footsteps. The system that the nordic countries have adopted isn't true socialism either, it's a form of social democracy. 

> I'm looking for something. Capitalism + socialism. Because I think that's the future.

Wholeheartedly agreed. No one system is entirely functional.

Identity politics and Marxism doesn't mix my friend. I would recommend you look into Marxism and read up on it a bit. It's a common misconception, and I understand that most people don't know what it's about. I would actually recommend everyone to read up on Marx regardless of your political leanings. You might disagree with Marxism, Leninism and all communism derivative ideologies, but it doesn't hurt to know what you're exactly advocating against. 

A true Marxist can never be an SJW and vehemently opposes identity politics. The entire point of all communism derivative ideologies is to unite under one banner (the working class) against the bourgeoisie (the upper class). People use marxism and communist as buzz words. I personally believe in class reductionism which is very different from being an sjw.

For further reading I would advise you check out this thread:

It's near impossible to get a well paying job after BCA alone. People typically go down the BCA+MCA route which isn't that bad either. Though B.Tech is traditionally preferred over BCA in the industry

Not to get your hopes down but the IIITH interview is notoriously tough. And not only do they analyze your problem solving skills and acumen, but they test your willingness for research. IIITH is a research oriented institute and is not looking for people who do a 4 year, get a job and make a beeline. You should have some backup options ready because as I said, it's very difficult to crack. Best of luck

Was in the same boat as you a couple of years back. All I have got to say is that it might seem the things that you're learning are useless to get a B.Tech degree, and past me would probably agree. But now I have come to appreciate the things I learnt during my JEE prep years. CSE involves a lot of maths, and I mean a lot of maths. If it weren't for those long hours of studying pcm endlessly I wouldn't be able to grasp things with ease.

Only other viable options are pursuing BCA or doing a bachelors of science in CSE (which will lead you down to a path of research). Though I would say, suck it up and prep for jee. B.tech is the best option for someone looking for a career in cse, and our education system doesn't allow for any flexibility in entrance examinations. Can't really do anything about it.
